title: ～という — called ～, named ～
summary: Used to give the name of something the listener may not know: “a ～ called X.” The name goes before という and the thing it names goes after. It is common for introducing people, places, shops, dishes and works.

patterns.form: 名前 ＋ という ＋ 名詞
patterns.gloss: name + という + noun (「さくら」という花)

body.p: Put the name in front of という and the category word after it: 「すし」という料理 (a dish called sushi). The speaker uses it when the thing is new to the listener or to introduce it briefly. In writing, a name is often put in 「」.
In conversation it is often shortened to という → って or ていう (田中さんっていう人). The same words also appear in other patterns such as ～ということ, so look at what comes before and after.

examples.ja: 「すし」という料理（りょうり）を食（た）べたことがありますか。
examples.romaji: 「Sushi」 to iu ryōri o tabeta koto ga arimasu ka.
examples.tr: Have you ever eaten a dish called “sushi”?

examples.ja: 「さくら」という名前（なまえ）の花（はな）を知（し）っていますか。
examples.romaji: 「Sakura」 to iu namae no hana o shitte imasu ka.
examples.tr: Do you know a flower called “sakura”?

examples.ja: 駅（えき）の近（ちか）くに「ひかり」というホテルがあります。
examples.romaji: Eki no chikaku ni 「Hikari」 to iu hoteru ga arimasu.
examples.tr: There is a hotel called “Hikari” near the station.

pitfalls: The name comes first: 「さくら」という花, not 花という「さくら」.
Use it for something the listener may not know. For well-known things just say the noun.
